title: Kamsasura Khandana - Sahana - Matya - Paidala Gurumurti Sastri
name: Kamsasura Khandana

ragas.name: Sahana
ragas.was: Sahana - S R2 G2 M1 P M1 D2 N1 S’ - S’ N1 D2 P M1 G2 M1 R2 G2 R2 S

sections.title: Lyrics
lyrics: kamsAsura khanDana jayarEy murArEy gopikAjAra navaneetha chora yAdavAbdhi chandhra krupAsAndhra
narakAnthaka rukmiNi sathyabhAma vilasitha vENunAdhapriyurEy surasEvya pAhimAm
shAna rAgam kAmbhoji janyam kampitha gAndhAram dheerga madhyama chathushruthi dhaivatha kaishiki nishAdha kampitha aalasitham
vakra sampoorNam gurumoorthEy chidhroopi arjuna sArathEy bhAshAnga rAgam shruNujaya krupAlo

text: You are the one who killed the demon kamsa, the one who killed mura, the one who steals the hearts of the gOpeekaas just as you steal butter. You are brilliant among the yaadavaas. You are so merciful. You destroyed narakaasura. You love playing the flute and being playful with rukmiNi and satyabhamaa. You save sages, Lord Krishna. Victory to you.

This is Sahanaa raga, derived from HarikaambhOji. It has trembling movements of the swara 'ga', a long stay on the swara 'ma', the swara 'da' that sits next to sudda daivata, and the swara 'ni' that is near to daivata. Playing the swaras gives the pleasure of listening to smooth movements between them. This is a propitiated raga, played even with zig-zag movement on all swaras. O Lord Krishna, listen to this subject-oriented raga. With your kindness, provide us with victory.

You are the one who killed the demon (asura) kamsa (kaMsa), the one who killed (arae) mura (muraa), the one who steals the hearts of the gOpeekaas (gOpeekaa jaara) just as you steal (chOra) butter (navneeta). You are brilliant (chandra) among the yaadavaas (yaadavaabdi). You are as merciful (kRpaa) as an ocean (saNdra). You destroyed (aNtaka) narakaasura (naraka). You love (priyure) playing the flute (vENunaada) and being playful (vilAsita) with rukmiNi and satyabhaamaa. You protect deities (sura sEvya); protect (pAhi) me (mAm).

This is Sahanaa raga, derived (janyaM) from HarikaambhOji. It has trembling (kaMpita) movements of the swara 'ga' (gaandharaM), a long (deergha) stay on the swara 'ma' (madhyamaM), the swara 'da' that sits next to sudda daivata (chaturSRti daivata), and the swara 'ni' that is near to daivata (kaiSiki nishaada). Playing (lasitaM) the swaras gives the pleasure of listening to smooth oscillations (kaMpita) between them. This is a propitiated raga, played even with zig-zag (vakra) movement on all (sampoorNam) swaras. O Lord Krishna (chidrUpArjunasArathE), listen (SruNu) to this subject-oriented (bhaashAnga) raga. With your kindness (kRpA LO), provide us with victory (jaya).
